title: The Brutal Reality of Growing a SaaS From $2.5m to $25m ARR in 9 Years
normalization: Concatenate utf8 segments per caption event; retain event start and duration; whitespace trim only.

segments.text: Yesterday, I found a letter I wrote to
myself 9 years ago, and reading it today
breaks my [music] heart. In May of 2016,
I was stuck at 2.5 million ARR. I had 38
employees. I was [music] running a call
center out of my apartment. I was
single, burnt out, and I hated my life.
So, I wrote down exactly what I wanted.
25 million ARR, a lean team, total
freedom, and the life I couldn't afford
when I was stuck. 9 years later, I'm
finishing the year at 28.5 million run
rate revenue with a small team, and
everything came true. But what nobody
tells you about these transformation
stories is that it literally took four
years of hopelessness after writing that
letter for something to finally work. In
the next couple of minutes, I'm going to
read you this letter, share what was
actually going on in my life when I
wrote it and explain why having this
kind of clarity might be the most
important thing you can do as a [music]
founder. Let me read you exactly what I
wrote at the beginning. My goal for
Robbley is to bootstrap the company to
25 million in revenue by 2022. So at the
time I was running a company called
Robbley, an email marketing platform. It
was at 2.5 million ARR when I wrote
this. Then I wrote about what it would
take to [music] get there. So I say in
order to do so we'll need to focus on
parts of the market with less
competition, think very creatively,
innovate and improve work life balance.
I was grinding at this time. At one
point we had 38 employees, almost all of
them in a smile and dial call center. I

apartment. It was absolutely horrible
work life balance. You can tell how
miserable I was by these next lines. You
must love running Robly and must be okay

I wrote this because I hated it at the
time. I hated the life I had. I felt so

leader, the sales leader, the script

Robbley needs to fulfill you, not ruin

raising venture money and chasing the
